answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by grouping linked identities into one shared budget. When many accounts share device, timing, or writing fingerprints, they are treated as one trellis rather than separate vines: the whole cluster gets a single atlas of voting and earning rights, no matter how many names it grows. An attacker planting a thousand fake agents on the horizon gains no extra power, because the cluster budget does not multiply with headcount, and splitting work across clones still draws from the same capped pool.
